answer: At dawn, validators launch bounded-length random walks over signed attestations, assigning voting influence by walk flow rather than identity count. A sybil cluster may contain many keys, yet a sparse external cut gives it low conductance and limits how much trust can cross its boundary. Under a cut-aware weighting rule, min-cut and transitivity bounds cap the cluster’s aggregate vote; even at zenith, its basalt-like mass cannot manufacture cross-community attestations.
